extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in censorship, journalism, Minecraft, and digital rights
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article describing The Uncensored Library — a Minecraft server and map project that stores banned journalism to circumvent censorship. The page covers the project's purpose, design, format, access methods, content selection, and reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project purpose / goal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Uncensored Library is an attempt to circumvent censorship in countries without freedom of the press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The project stores banned reporting from multiple countries so readers in restrictive environments can access censored journalism; framing as a means to bypass censorship is the central stated purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of content
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters Without Borders published the project and selected the articles displayed within the library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The texts are banned reporting from specific countries (Mexico, Russia, Vietnam, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Brazil, Belarus, Iran, Eritrea, and the United States), implying a curated selection process by the publisher/advocacy organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country-specific organization (Country wings)
rubrics_metrics.description: An entire wing is given to each country, each containing several banned articles placed in virtual books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each country's wing contains multiple articles and interior architecture that symbolizes that country's unique situation and journalistic challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format of texts — in-game book items
rubrics_metrics.description: The texts within the library are contained in in-game book items, which can be opened and placed on stands to be read by multiple players at once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This specifies the in-game medium chosen to present articles and the interactive affordances (openable, placeable on stands for group reading).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Each country's texts are available in English and the original language the article was written in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides bilingual access to the articles to reach both international and native-language readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design style / architectural symbolism
rubrics_metrics.description: The library is a large-scale project built using a neoclassical architectural style intended to resemble well-established institutions (e.g., New York Public Library, Thomas Jefferson Building) and to stylistically allude to the authoritarian structures the project aims to subvert.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design choices are explicitly tied to symbolic meaning: referencing recognized library architecture to lend gravitas while alluding to authoritarian structures the project critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale / technical magnitude
rubrics_metrics.description: The library uses over 12.5 million Minecraft blocks; one Minecraft block is equal to one cubic meter in-game.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicates the project's physical (in‑game) scale and technical ambition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Two ways to access the library are to download a map from the official website, or to connect to their Minecraft server.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents practical access routes for users wishing to reach the content; implies availability via both offline map and live server.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rooms / features (Press Freedom Index & memorials)
rubrics_metrics.description: The library contains a central room listing the Press Freedom Index and state of freedom of the press of every country covered by the index; the Mexican section contains memorials for reporters who were killed due to their writings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These curated features provide contextual data (index) and commemorative elements (memorials), linking content to broader metrics and human costs of censorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content themes
rubrics_metrics.description: The articles generally discuss censorship, unjust punishment, and other critiques of the writer's government; additional rooms cover topical issues such as the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the topical focus of included works and confirms that thematic rooms (e.g., COVID-19 impact across multiple countries) are used to illustrate specific journalistic challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project timeline / release context
rubrics_metrics.description: The library was released on 12 March 2020, the World Day Against Cyber Censorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release timing ties the project to an international advocacy day, indicating strategic launch context for visibility and solidarity with digital-censorship awareness efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creators, roles, and attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The structure was built by Berlin DDB and BlockWorks, while .monks and Reporters Without Borders published the project; Reporters Without Borders also selected the articles displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies division of labor between creative/build teams and publisher/curator, important for provenance and credibility of the curated content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reception and recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: After launch the project went viral across social media, was featured by many media outlets, and received a 2022 Peabody Award for the Interactive category; Peabody described it as 'a monument to press freedom and an innovative back door for access to censored content.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents external validation and media impact, which function as evaluative indicators of the project's influence and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository size / content count (historical snapshot)
rubrics_metrics.description: In March 2020, the library contained over 200 different books; additional wings and rooms (e.g., a United States wing added in 2026) have been added over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides quantitative snapshots of the project's content scope and indicates that the library can be expanded to cover new jurisdictions or themes.
